shouldFix.title: Decision 1 says the recorded successor binds NOTHING while Decision 2 says the gates now name the classes, so the entry leaves the operative standing of the naming unsettled — and departs from D-086's own formulation for this same artifact family without saying why
shouldFix.finding: Decision 1 reads 'Record gate-harness-naming.v6.json as the D-086 successor candidate owed by D-144. The candidate binds NOTHING.' Decision 2 reads 'DR-G21 now names DR-133 NT-1, NT-2, NT-6 as executing there. DR-G20 now names DR-133 NT-4, NT-7 as executing there.' Those cannot both be read strictly. If the recorded candidate binds nothing, nothing now names anything; if the gates now name the classes, the recording did more than bind nothing. The question is not academic — it is the one the D-144 to v6 to D-145 chain exists to answer, because D-056 gate 3 asks whether each remainder is already named at a condition-4 obligation with an owner. A later cycle reading Decision 1 could conclude the riding classes are still named nowhere operative, which would nullify the chain; reading Decision 2 it could conclude the opposite. The predecessor for this exact artifact family shows the intended posture and does not use the disclaimer. D-086 is titled 'Record gate-harness-naming.v3 as the condition-4 naming candidate' and its Decision records v3 as the naming candidate without any binds-nothing clause — measured, that phrase does not occur in D-086 — and the effect of that recording is visible in live file 08, whose condition-4 cell cites '(D-086 / D-088 / D-102)' as where the identifiers are named and whose DR-G21 harness cell reads 'named: harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment (D-086; …)'. Note too that file 08's G21 cell does not mention CC-1..CC-11: the DR-102 class naming lives in the D-086 artifact, which is exactly where v6 puts the NT naming, so Decision 2's 'now names' is true in the same sense as the precedent. The defect is that Decision 1 imports the binds-NOTHING formula from the design-contract-candidate branch — D-136, D-138, D-144 — into a naming recording where D-086 deliberately did not use it, and then Decision 2 asserts the naming has taken effect.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: Nothing about DR-133's readiness is misstated. The row stays OPEN, nothing is marked SATISFIED, gates 2 and 3 are said not to hold, and the condition-4 effect is correctly zero. The ambiguity is about what the recording establishes, not about any measured fact.
shouldFix.repair: Follow D-086. Drop 'The candidate binds NOTHING' from Decision 1, or replace it with the posture D-086 used — record the successor as the condition-4 naming candidate, with 'Naming is not execution. Not QUALIFIED', which Decision 2 already says. Then state plainly what this recording establishes: after this entry the five riding NT classes are named at DR-G20 and DR-G21 in the same sense D-086's recording names the harness identifiers file 08 cites, and gate 3 nonetheless still fails because NT-3 and NT-5 are named nowhere. That last clause keeps Decision 3 true while removing the contradiction.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Twelve attacks run, one landed. Custody is clean: e5394376 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 1ac85c7, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, and all seven file pins plus the commit pin reproduce. Everything measurable holds. The naming split — NT-1, NT-2, NT-6 at DR-G21 and NT-4, NT-7 at DR-G20 — matches v6's amended executes fields and the join's riding map exactly; NT-3 and NT-5 stay leftover-design; the condition-4 statement is the one I asked v6 to make and verified there, and it matches live file 08, whose condition-4 row reads MET with every assurance stage below QUALIFIED; the readiness recital matches at 4 of 32; the no-cell-edit branch claim holds, since D-086's own entry says it does not edit file 08; and my verdict is represented exactly as ACCEPT 0/0 with no advisories attributed to me. What blocks is that Decision 1 and Decision 2 pull opposite ways. Decision 1 says the recorded candidate binds NOTHING; Decision 2 says the two gates now name the five classes. Read strictly they cannot both hold, and the question is precisely the one this chain exists to answer, because D-056 gate 3 asks whether each remainder is already named at a condition-4 obligation with an owner — and both gates do carry owners in file 08. The predecessor settles what the intended posture is: D-086 records gate-harness-naming.v3 as the condition-4 naming candidate and uses no binds-nothing clause at all, and the effect of that recording is visible in live file 08, which cites D-086 as where the identifiers are named. Note also that file 08's G21 cell never mentions CC-1..CC-11, so the class-level naming lives in the D-086 artifact — exactly where v6 puts the NT naming, which makes Decision 2's 'now names' true in the same sense as the precedent. The fix is to follow D-086: drop the imported binds-NOTHING formula and say what the recording establishes — the five riding classes are named at G20 and G21 as D-086's recording names the identifiers file 08 cites, and gate 3 still fails because NT-3 and NT-5 are named nowhere. One note on method: the phrase 'binds NOTHING' is split across a line break in the source, so a naive search reports zero occurrences; I found it only after whitespace-normalising, and I mention it because the same trap would hide it from anyone checking this entry by grep.
